_note: UI strings for the BTF module (notifications / review editor / text view / validation notices). Key names are fixed in code; missing entries fall back to the default language. {0} {1} are placeholders.
name: BTF files
cmd.open.failed: Failed to open the BTF view: {0}
cmd.export.placeholder: Choose the BTF file to export
cmd.export.readFailed: Failed to read the BTF file: {0}
view.broken:
; Broken view address: the source file cannot be resolved.
; Reopen it with "WRSR: Open BTF view".
report.title: ; BTF file · read-only view
report.subtitle: ; Parsed by "Workers & Resources Mod Toolkit". This view cannot be edited — export JSON first to change anything.
report.unparseable: ; Status     unparsable: the header is incomplete
report.entries: ; Entries    {0}{1}; definition table {2} ~ {3} bytes ({4} bytes each)
report.escapes: ; Escapes    In the text column, \ \t \n \r and non-printable characters are shown escaped; JSON / CSV export keeps the original text
report.range: ; Range      only the first {0} of {1} entries are listed —
report.rangeNote: ;            the limit is the wrsr.btf.view.maxEntries setting (export is never limited)
report.moreProblems: ; …{0} more notices of the same kind are not listed
parse.tooShort: The file is only {0} bytes — not even the {1}-byte header fits.
parse.lengthMismatch: The header says the file length is {0} bytes, but the file is {1} bytes{2}.
parse.negativeCharCount: The header's text-area character count is negative ({0}) — the header is corrupt.
parse.negativeCount: The header's entry count is negative ({0}) — the header is corrupt.
parse.tableTooBig: The header says {0} entries (needing a {1}-byte definition table), but the file is only {2} bytes and can hold {3}. The table below lists just those {3}.
parse.oddTextBytes: The text area runs from byte {0} to the end — {1} bytes, which is odd. The text area is UTF-16, so the byte count should be even.
parse.noTextArea: The text area should start at byte {0}, but the file is only {1} bytes — nothing after the definition table is actually in the file (the file was truncated, or the header's entry count is wrong).
parse.entry.badLength: Entry {0} (id={1}): the length field is {2} — it is an int16, so 32767 reads back as a negative number. This entry is treated as empty text.
parse.entry.badOffset: Entry {0} (id={1}): charOffset is negative ({2}) — this definition is corrupt. The entry is treated as empty text.
parse.entry.outOfRange: Entry {0} (id={1}): the text needs {3} bytes starting at byte {2}, but the file is only {4} bytes — out of range. This entry is treated as empty text.
parse.entry.notTerminated: Entry {0} (id={1}): length says {2} characters, but that position is not \0 (it is U+{3}) — length or charOffset probably do not match the content.
parse.entry.badSurrogates: Entry {0} (id={1}): the text contains {2} unpaired UTF-16 surrogates, shown as U+FFFD (�) — those code units are broken in the original file.
parse.sumMismatch: The header says the text area holds {0} characters, but the {1} entries add up to {2} (each entry is length + 1, with no padding between entries) — a difference of {3}. The text area may have been edited, or the entry count / length fields are wrong.
parse.duplicatedIds: There are {0} duplicated ids (the same id maps to several texts). The game looks up text by id, so only one of them takes effect.
build.entriesNotArray: BTF: entries must be an array
build.badId: Entry {0}: id is not a 32-bit integer ({1}).
build.textTooLong: Entry {0} (id={1}): the text is {2} characters, over the {3} limit of the length field (int16). The format cannot store longer text.
build.tooLarge: The generated file would be {0} bytes, over the limit of the header's file-length field (int32).
json.noEntries: The JSON has no entries array (an exported file should have one; a bare array is accepted too).
json.itemMissing: Item {0} is missing id or text.
json.note: Workers & Resources BTF export. Edit the text fields, then rebuild with "WRSR: Build BTF from JSON"; nothing other than id and text needs to be maintained here (charOffset / length are recomputed in order by the tool).
pick.otherDesc: Not in the list? Pick one yourself
pick.addPlaceholder: Pick another .btf as a comparison column (aligned by id; you can edit it right here)
doc.alreadyAdded: That file is already in the comparison.
doc.addFailed: Failed to read the comparison file: {0}
confirm.layout: {0} does not use the standard layout (the text area has holes, or entries were reordered). Overwriting will lay the text area out in the official order — not a single translation changes, but **the bytes do**.
confirm.loss: {0} had {1} broken UTF-16 code units (unpaired surrogates) while parsing; they have already been replaced with U+FFFD (�) in memory. Writing will store those replacements — the original code units will be gone.
confirm.fresh: {0} was changed by another program after you opened it (the version on disk is newer). Overwrite it with what you have here?
save.savedAs: Saved a copy as {0} (neither the original nor the comparison columns were touched)
revert.confirm: Discard all unsaved changes and re-parse what is on disk?
revert.done: Re-parsed from what is on disk
reload.confirm: There are unsaved changes; re-parsing would discard them. Continue?
copy.ok: BTF review: copied to the clipboard
copy.failed: Failed to copy to the clipboard.
error.moduleHint: (usually a function missing from some module's module.exports; the extension host may also need a reload)
page.title: BTF review
page.resizeTitle: Drag up or down to resize the edit area
page.cell.emptyTitle: the translation for id {0} is an empty string
